beds.why: The street at night: crickets and still air.
Daylight: birds, open air, the town awake.
The party on the other side of the glass.
A bedroom with two speakers in it.
The birthday party, one metre away.
An empty kitchen: it has to be almost silent.
The room where all the practice happens.
A hundred people in a room with no windows.
Back outside, and the night is the same night.

sfx.why: Round to his back, the speaker in his arms, the lit door in front of him.
The third hush behind him.
The tape rewind: the same doorway, four years earlier.
The rewind running out as the daylight lands.
The cut to him arriving with the speaker.
His feet on the road.
Into the party behind the glass.
The room going up inside, muffled by the window.
Out to him on the step, hopeful.
He says it in one breath and it lands.
His feet taking him away from the door.
Into the bedroom: the smallest room in the film.
The chair he sits down on.
The little green light on the cabinet.
Into the birthday: the fairy lights, the cake, the borrowed setup.
The yard, happy, before he plays.
The fairy lights overhead.
The needle going down on the record.
Two bars play.
The needle skips.
His hands grabbing at the wrong cable.
The feedback squeal, and forty faces turning.
The moment it stops being his party.
The whole yard goes quiet, and the floor goes out from under him.
Put on my phone: four words, not even meant badly.
The phone starts playing.
The cable coming off the floor.
The yard dancing to a phone behind him.
Into the kitchen, later.
The cloth on the table.
The plate he moves out of the way.
Down to the record and the sleeve.
The sleeve opening.
The record sliding back in, carefully.
Into the montage.
The needle down, first try.
And it is wrong.
The same try, closer.
The hand shaking on the record.
Writing 84 on a label.
The pencil.
The brush, and the beat he is counting.
Beats, tapped out on his teeth.
To the window at night, and the town asleep.
Air moving in the room.
Mixing one-handed.
The record spinning up.
His eyes shut, headphones on.
The record turning under his hands.
The lamp off: only the mixer lights.
One light on the desk.
The word on the wall.
The tape pressed flat.
Dawn through the window.
He is asleep sitting up, headphones still on.
Down to the stack of records.
The sleeves, counted.
The last record, and the room finally moving with him.
The needle down and it lands.
The room opening up.
Out to the street, and the queue at THE DOOR.
The club, from outside.
The queue shuffling on the pavement.
In to him behind the booth.
A record already running.
Thank you, flat, no smile.
And it is gone.
The three of them push in through the door.
Their feet on the dance floor.
The shout, and the room answering it.
A glass put down on the bar.
The record lifted off.
The next one, already in his hand.
To their faces, having the night of their lives.
Their cheer, for the music.
Everything dropping away so one word can be heard.
Bedroom.
The needle comes down hard.
The whole room goes up.
The drop.
Alone in the booth, and no smile at all.
The lights going round him.
His feet, passing them.
A nod each way, and neither of them places him.
He keeps walking, out of the light.
And out of the town.
The last of the light, and the cut.
